accepted_scope_caveats.label: Open-ended Question 1 and Theorems 3–4
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The classification is conditional on a supplied three-item binary conditional-missingness graph, full joint support, no latent variables, and no response-to-substantive arrows.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: The claimed completeness and strict method frontier concern only the stated finite graph model; they make no graph-learning, boundary-law, continuous-variable, or latent-variable claim.

source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 6–7, Theorems 1–2; p. 8, lines 1113–1141, discussion and Conclusion
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Theorems 1–2 give the no-self-censoring/no-colluder sound-and-complete criterion for full-law identification. The paper explicitly states that full-law identification is sufficient but not necessary for target-law identification and leaves complete target-law characterization to future work.

source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 7–8, Proposition 1, Corollary 1, Proposition 2, Lemma 2; p. 8, Section 6
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Proposition 1 gives a sufficient partial-order grouped-fixing route for propensity identification, Corollary 1 obtains target-law identification when every needed propensity is identified, and the conclusion leaves efficient general search and completeness open.

source_verification_receipts.locator: p. 17, Theorem 1; pp. 30–31, Section 8, especially lines 1308–1322
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Theorem 1 is a sound identification-functional result for the intervention tree. Section 8 expressly says the algorithm is sound but incomplete, gives Appendix Figure E.2(a) as an odds-ratio-identifiable false negative, and identifies systematic sound-and-complete hybridization as an open direction.

source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 9–10, Theorem 1 and its full-rank linear-system derivation
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The categorical-colluder result identifies the relevant missingness component when each colluder matrix has full rank, using a Moore–Penrose inverse; it does not provide a graph-uniform target-law classification on rank-degenerate strata.

The paper states that the criss-cross structure prevents nonparametric target-law identification, while additional restrictions recover components; it is not a complete all-graph target-law classifier.

The paper reduces broad discrete causal problems to polynomial programs and provides numerical sharp bounds, including point identification at global completion; it does not extract graph-specific rational formulas or positive rational twin certificates.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Before Stage 0, publish the canonical edge-word list and the exact script or proof artifact reproducing the 12,800/204/34 partition; this makes the finite audit independently reproducible.
Add one worked residual row that exhibits the full route from graph word through exceptional-stratum test to either a rational functional or a positive rational twin family.

State an explicit corollary separating the finite Complete3 result from Guo and Nabi’s general incomplete tree: identify precisely which tree state or odds-ratio constructor supplies each strict inclusion.

recommended_next_step: Advance to Stage 0 with the residual dichotomy and Complete3 iff classification as the field-tier kernel; retain the odds regression and delta-method layer as regression and consequence results.
